scope: Minimal bibliographic import only for four screenshot items; no model extraction or reference import. Existing notes and status flags preserved.

items.title: An Agent-Based Approach to Modeling Online Social Influence
items.entry: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/An Agent-Based Approach to Modeling Online Social Influence.md
items.summary: Models how persuasion factors, profile counts and external events affect topic-message choices on a fixed follower network. Directly relevant to communication and exposure; it does not implement an opinion-state update or changing friendships.

items.title: An agent-based model of the development of friendship links within Facebook
items.entry: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/An agent-based model of the development of friendship links within Facebook.md
items.access: Publisher abstract available; full text is subscription restricted on publisher page.
items.summary: Uses Caltech Facebook friendship data and competing agent-based network-growth processes to assess student preferences and structural constraints. Personal preference plus social structure best matches the observed network. Direct overlap with evolving social ties; does not directly model recommender algorithms or integration outcomes.

items.title: An Agent-Based Model of Urgent Diffusion in Social Media
items.entry: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/An Agent-Based Model of Urgent Diffusion in Social Media.md
items.access: Full article and abstract openly readable at JASSS.
items.summary: Presents Bass and independent-cascade agent-based models of urgent information adoption, fit to four Twitter events. Network ties mediate peer diffusion while external shocks can dominate; useful for exposure/diffusion mechanisms, though it studies adoption rather than social integration or friendship formation.

items.title: Dynamic Social Networks in Agent-based Modelling: Increasingly Detailed Approaches of Network Initialisation and Network Dynamics
items.entry: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/Dynamic Social Networks in Agent-based Modelling- Increasingly Detailed Approaches of Network Initialisation and Network Dynamics.md
items.access: Open access dissertation PDF; browser retrieval returned a content-size error, but direct PDF URL and university bibliographic records are available.
items.summary: A dissertation focused on progressively detailed network initialization and dynamics in agent-based modelling, including social network structure and changing ties. Strong methodological and mechanism overlap for representing evolving social ties; it is not itself an evaluation of social-media recommendation algorithms.
